title: LibreFlow Annotate
summary: A self-hosted workspace with MCP and automation for labeling images and turning reviewed annotations into training datasets. Annotations can be drawn, reviewed, and versioned before export in formats including YOLO, COCO, and Pascal VOC. LibreFlow allows usage of a local detector for selected classes or point prompts to generate masks using the user's hardware; no more tokens or cloud inference!

problem: Inspection data is scattered across labeling tools, review notes, model scripts, and export utilities. That makes it harder to know what was reviewed and which dataset reached training, especially for sensitive images.
purpose: The goal was a local-first path from board images to reviewed annotations, immutable versions, and training exports while keeping source pixels and inference under operator control.
keyFeatures: Draw boxes, polygons, masks, and points. Reviewers can flag an individual annotation and restore earlier revisions.
Run a local detector for selected classes or use point prompts to generate a mask.
Choose project batches, set train/validation/test proportions, and preview preprocessing and augmentation before creating a version.
Export the same version for training in formats including YOLO, COCO, and Pascal VOC.
role: I designed the annotation workflow, implemented the front-end and back-end, and integrated a local detector for selected classes. I also created the versioning system and export formats.
technicalHighlights: Fully working annotation and review workflow with versioning and export used on actual projects.
Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) annotation working and implemented significantly reducing annotation workload.
Local inference for selected classes and point prompts to generate masks using the user's hardware.
Versioning system that records source images, split assignments, transformation settings, and file checksums for each version.
Tiling for large images to allow labeling of high-resolution images without downscaling.
Augmentation and preprocessing of images for training export, including rotation, flipping, color jitter, and random cropping.
Allows for multiple users to work on the same project with different roles and permissions.
Saving uploaded images as dataset to allow reuse of the same images for different projects and versions.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: A second model pass can duplicate objects an inspector has already labeled.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: The inspector chooses which model classes to run. Existing annotations stay in place while the new predictions are added.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: A training export can be difficult to trace once the working project changes.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Each version records its source images, split assignments, transformation settings, and file checksums.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Small components can disappear when a high-resolution board photo is resized for a detector. A component on a tile boundary can also appear twice.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: LibreFlow crops overlapping tiles at native resolution, translates each prediction back to board coordinates, and merges overlapping boxes of the same class. Reviewers inspect the results on the original image.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Drawing an irregular outline by hand is slow, and a first model prediction can include part of a neighboring component.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: An annotator can give the local segmentation model foreground and background point prompts, inspect the proposed contour, and edit the mask before saving.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: A crop or rotation can move a label off its object. Augmented copies can also leak into the validation set if splitting happens too late.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: The version builder assigns source images to splits first, applies geometric changes to the image and its annotations together, and generates augmented copies only for training.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: An approval can become stale when a collaborator edits a label after review.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Editing submitted or approved annotations returns the image to work in progress. Open issues block approval, and the project owner or assigned reviewer can check the correction against the revision history.

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Two projects may need the same board photos for different labeling tasks.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: A team can save the source images as a dataset, then import them as a new batch with optional tags. The new batch starts unlabeled, so its annotations can evolve independently.

resultsImpact: Eliminated the need to use other annotation platforms and tools for labeling, reviewing, and exporting datasets that charges usage, publicizes datasets, and limited to existing features.
A reviewer can trace a training image back to its source and inspect how it was transformed.
A team can export a saved version again while continuing to label new images in the project.
Delivered industry-level datasets used in training CV and ML models during my tenure of employment.
Significant reduction in annotation workload by using model-assisted labeling and review.
An annotator can add predictions for a missing class or refine a single mask locally while keeping earlier labels available for review.
Reviewers can attach a correction to the affected annotation and see when a later edit reopens an approved image.
A second project can reuse a board-image collection and its tags while keeping its labeling decisions separate.
lessonsLearned: Creating your own platform for labeling and reviewing images is a big investment, but it can pay off when you need to control your data and workflow.
Optimizing the annotation workflow for a specific use case can significantly reduce the time and effort required to label images.
Show original and augmented image counts separately. A training multiplier is easier to interpret when the user can see both counts.
Keep the board visible at the current zoom when jumping between annotations so reviewers can judge each label in context.
Tile size and overlap are review decisions as well as model settings. A small component at the edge of a crop may need the neighboring tile to be recognizable.
Split at the source-image level. Two rotated views of the same board should never land on opposite sides of a training and validation split.
An approval belongs to a particular revision. Returning edited images to the review queue keeps that promise visible to collaborators.
Annotators can be more productive when they can see the model's predictions and correct them in place rather than drawing from scratch.
A local model can be used to generate masks for a single object or class, but it is not a replacement for human review.
Model assistance is most useful when the annotator can narrow the request to one class or one object and correct the result in place.
